text:
jessica_support: heads-up — acme reported a ~3x invoice jump last night after a brief auth outage. customer sent logs showing many duplicate completions, asking for quick audit.

sam_billing: can you paste the invoice id + customer id? i need to correlate ledger entries before I file an adjustment.

jessica_support: customer id = acct_0A1B2C, invoice = inv_2026-02-18-99. they included a server log snippet, key section below:
```
2026-02-18T21:04:02Z POST /v1/generate 200 tokens=102 body_hash=abc123 client_req_id=xyz
2026-02-18T21:04:08Z POST /v1/generate 200 tokens=102 body_hash=abc123 client_req_id=xyz
2026-02-18T21:04:15Z POST /v1/generate 200 tokens=102 body_hash=abc123 client_req_id=xyz
```
looks like the client retried after refresh and the gateway accepted each attempt as separate usage. no Idempotency-Key present.

mike_sre: i pulled gateway traces. confirmed three distinct ingestion events within ~15s for same payload. gateway only dedupes when Idempotency-Key header exists, and SDK didn't set one.

mike_sre: quick repro i ran locally:
```
# simulate expired token then client retry after refresh
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <expired>" -d @prompt.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate || true
# client obtains new token and retries with same body (no Idempotency-Key)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <new>" -d @prompt.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
that produced two distinct ledger writes. same payload, different auth flow -> double billing.

anna_engineering: given many clients won't set Idempotency-Key, can we add a short server-side dedupe based on body hash+route with TTL (eg 60s)? that would catch replay-after-auth cases without breaking legitimate retries that change payload.

mike_sre: i prototyped a lightweight filter in the gateway: compute sha256(body)+route -> check in-memory cache (ttl=60s). if hit, return cached response id and avoid re-executing model. preliminary tests look good.

deploy-bot: canary rollout of gateway dedupe filter to cluster-2 scheduled for 2026-02-19T03:00Z (rolling, 10% traffic). logs forwarded to #eng-runtime.

sam_billing: once you confirm which ledger rows are duplicates, i'll file the credit/refund. need ledger uuids and token counts.

jessica_support: ledger rows for acct_0A1B2C (same prompt): ledg_01a, ledg_01b, ledg_01c — each 102 tokens. i've attached the CSV to ticket SUP-5234.

sam_billing: refund/credit issued for two duplicate events. applied to inv_2026-02-18-99. accounting case #ACCT-8891. notified customer.

jessica_support: customer replied: "Thanks, invoice looks correct now — appreciate the fast turnaround!" :thumbsup: :tada:

anna_engineering: follow-up items: 1) add Idempotency-Key guidance to SDK docs, 2) ship SDK default idempotency header in 1.4.0, 3) keep server dedupe TTL conservative (60s) and monitor for legitimate dedupe false positives.

mike_sre: added metric duplicate_detected{route="/v1/generate"} and a small dashboard. alert threshold = 5 duplicates/min beyond baseline for 15m. will monitor during canary.

jessica_support: closing thread. linked internal ticket: https://internal.redwood/insights/SUP-5234 — please ping here if canary shows any issues.
